title: Choose the InnovProcure visual direction
question: The operating brief is set: five roles, real procurement workflows, and a deep-navy, teal, and restrained-amber palette. Which visual system should carry that work?

options.label: Civic Wayfinding
options.thesis: A civic wayfinding system makes the route from public need to scaled procurement legible at a glance.
options.viewport: The existing role-aware sidebar stays familiar; a live dashboard pairs real procurement indicators with a clearly labeled, eight-stage pathway and its current counts. Flat wayfinding markers identify each module and stage without replacing standard controls.
options.risk: Route language must not blur the distinct review tasks in each module.

raised.raise: Keep stage and metric comparisons disciplined in aligned columns so density stays readable.

options.label: State Gazette Index
options.lineage: Maharashtra government resolutions and public notices
options.thesis: A clear public record puts authority, status, and the next action in their proper order.
options.viewport: Keep the role-aware sidebar and familiar controls; lead with the selected module, its real workflow summary, and a prioritized queue of the records that need action.
options.risk: A record-first hierarchy can feel document-heavy if it buries the live workflow.

options.label: Public Service Timetable
options.lineage: Public transport timetables and departure boards
options.thesis: A disciplined timetable rhythm makes many live stages easy to scan in one pass.
options.viewport: Standard navigation and controls frame a live dashboard; the stage summary and next-action queue use aligned columns, with amber reserved for items that need attention.
options.case: Strong workflow clarity; it holds product clarity while civic wayfinding better identifies the Maharashtra public-service context.
options.risk: Too much timetable structure could make detail-heavy forms feel cramped.

options.label: Metro Service Tiles
options.thesis: Flat, labeled tiles give each workspace module a clear place and state.
options.viewport: A familiar sidebar and top bar anchor the dashboard; a compact grid of labeled workflow tiles surfaces current records, actions, and status without horizontal scrolling or hidden controls.
options.case: Strong audience recognition and product clarity; civic wayfinding offers a more coherent signature across dense forms and tables.
options.risk: Oversized tile labels could compete with real data in dense modules.

options.label: Catalog Wall
options.thesis: A catalog of expandable tiles makes each available record feel like a selectable destination.
options.viewport: The standard shell stays intact, but a dense dashboard becomes a wall of record cards.
options.case: Does not identify with public procurement work and weakens side-by-side comparison.
options.kept: Make the currently selected record unmistakable.
options.risk: A card wall hides important comparison fields.

options.label: Area Map
options.thesis: Separate color areas distinguish the different parts of a complex system.
options.viewport: Standard modules are grouped as distinct regions around a central dashboard.
options.case: The map metaphor does not help visitors complete the platform’s record-based tasks.
options.kept: Use clear visual boundaries between distinct work areas.
options.risk: Spatial grouping can make cross-stage handoffs harder to follow.

options.label: Folded Case File
options.lineage: Cassette inlay cards and timed tracklists
options.thesis: A compact, ordered list makes an item's full history easy to follow.
options.viewport: The dashboard is arranged as a compact case file with records grouped by stage.
options.case: The artifact does not fit the public-sector procurement context and the fold metaphor adds no value.
options.kept: Preserve an explicit, readable sequence of dated actions.
options.risk: A fold-based structure would hide details behind an unnecessary interaction.

options.label: Live Departure Board
options.thesis: A dense status board brings changing states into one shared glance.
options.viewport: A standard dashboard shows a dense live board of procurement and review events.
options.case: It makes the product read like a transit instrument rather than a role-based procurement workspace.
options.kept: Keep changing and delayed states easy to distinguish.
options.risk: Per-character motion would distract and would not improve task completion.

canonCard.label: The government workspace standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar role-based workspace keeps records, controls, and next actions easy to find.
canonCard.viewport: A stable left navigation, contextual header, and working dashboard with real service data, filters, and a clear next action.
canonCard.risk: The familiar arrangement needs careful craft to avoid feeling like a template.
